statement: The supplied sources genuinely contain nothing to derive. Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence is defined between probability distributions P and Q as D_KL(P || Q) = sum_x P(x) log(P(x) / Q(x)) (or for continuous distributions, integral p(x) log(p(x) / q(x)) dx); the supplied source contains no derivation and states only that cross-entropy and KL divergence are identical up to an additive constant.

symbols.meaning: Kullback–Leibler divergence from Q to P

properties.property: Cross-entropy and KL divergence are identical up to an additive constant.
properties.why: Cross-entropy differs from KL divergence only by an additive constant when the reference distribution is fixed.

properties.property: In engineering literature, the principle of minimizing KL divergence (Kullback's 'Principle of Minimum Discrimination Information') is often called the Principle of Minimum Cross-Entropy (MCE), or Minxent.
properties.why: Minimizing KL divergence is equivalent to minimizing cross-entropy because they differ only by an additive constant.

assumptions.assumption: The reference distribution is fixed when comparing cross-entropy and KL divergence.
assumptions.breaks_when: The reference distribution varies with respect to the optimization parameters, so the additive term is no longer constant.

assumptions.assumption: The support of P is contained in the support of Q (absolute continuity).
assumptions.breaks_when: Q(x) = 0 for some x where P(x) > 0, causing division by zero inside the logarithm.

failure_modes.mode: Equivalence between MCE and minimum KL divergence fails
failure_modes.signature: Minimizing cross-entropy yields an optimal distribution different from minimizing KL divergence
failure_modes.cause: The reference distribution is not held constant, making the additive difference parameter-dependent.

failure_modes.mode: Undefined divergence or divergence to infinity
failure_modes.signature: Evaluation yields infinity or undefined values
failure_modes.cause: The approximating distribution assigns zero probability to an event that has non-zero probability under the reference distribution.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so kl_divergence is recorded as a definition
